key_insight: The paper uses reinforcement learning to robustify a nominal trajectory with an affine feedback policy, aiming for chance-constrained feasibility without assuming a specific uncertainty distribution.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical framework for spacecraft and guidance problems where uncertainty can be sampled but not reliably modeled, while still controlling fuel cost and constraint satisfaction.
method: Compute a deterministic nominal trajectory offline as the baseline.
Train RL to add a feedforward correction plus time-varying feedback gains.
Enforce probabilistic feasibility via rollout-based upper-tail quantiles and terminal spread via covariance penalties.
evidence_signal: The approach is evaluated on two different problems—a 3D multi-impulse Earth-Mars transfer and a stochastic atmospheric rocket landing—and tested under Gaussian, bounded uniform, and unseen disturbance cases.
watch_item: Performance depends on sampled rollouts and learned robustness terms, so feasibility and cost may be sensitive to training coverage and scenario mismatch.
paper_title: Distribution-Agnostic Robust Trajectory Optimization via Chance-Constrained Reinforcement Learning
